summary: Prefix lookup fallback to cold path causing repeat-prompt 504s and p99 latency spikes
description: Customers on Dedicated pools are seeing intermittent 504s and large p99 generation latencies for repeated prompts that should hit the prefix/KV cache. Symptoms started ~2026-03-09 after a runtime kernel selection change. Initial hypothesis: certain prefix keys are being misclassified as stale and routed to cold model path, causing heavy synchronous KV lookups and request timeouts.
impact: LexaHealth experiences elevated user-visible latency and sporadic failed responses for repeated-chat workflows. Affects a subset of traffic on their dedicated pool (estimated 5-8% of requests) and results in degraded experience for end-users; potential revenue impact for high-volume features.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use LexaHealth dedicated API key against us-east endpoint in prod
2) Send a chat sequence with a stable 120-token prefix (same prompt repeated in subsequent requests)
3) Observe initial successful warm responses, then intermittent 504s or p99 spikes on subsequent identical-prompts
4) Reproduce reliably by replaying captured traffic from 2026-03-09 14:00-16:00 UTC (recorded session ID in logs)
5) Capture request/response traces from tracing ID header x-rdwd-trace for affected requests

investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 09:15 - Support (Aisha): Confirmed LexaHealth dedicated pool shows p99 jumps correlated to prefix keys recorded in their replay logs.

2026-03-10 10:02 - SRE (Derek): Observed pattern where prefix entries are reported as expired by cache coordinator while downstream KV still serving shards; spikes follow an increase in concurrent warm starts after a kernel-selection deploy.

2026-03-10 12:30 - Eng (Mariana): Reproduced locally by toggling kernel selector flag; when kernel path changes, prefix cache TTL validation yields false-negative and enqueues cold fetches from persistent KV which are serialized, causing head-of-line blocking.

Hypothesis: Kernel selector change (opt-in int8 path) altered the cache key normalization (sequence-length bucket) leading to mismatch between in-memory prefix index and persisted KV keys. Result: cache coordinator marks prefix as stale, triggering concurrent cold fetches and long synchronous waits -> 504s.
Telemetry: Concurrent cold fetches per key observed up to 30; KV read p99 increased from 45ms to 2.9s for affected keys during incidents. Error budget breach risk for customer SLA.
workaround: 1) Roll back kernel selector change for LexaHealth dedicated pool (actioned 2026-03-10 15:00 UTC) to restore key normalization parity.
2) Temporarily increase cache coordinator dedup window to 10s to prevent multiple simultaneous cold fetches while full fix is developed.
3) Advise customer to throttle bursty automated replay workflows until we confirm stable behavior (applied rate-limit on route for 6 hours).
resolution_plan: Short-term (P0): Keep rollback in place and monitor p99 for 24h; verify no further 504s for repeated prompts.
Medium-term: Patch cache coordinator to use explicit key normalization that includes kernel-path metadata so kernel-selector changes do not flip cache identity.
Long-term: Add unit and e2e tests to validate cache key stability across kernel selector and quantization flags; add canary gating for kernel selector feature toggles.
Owners: Derek (SRE) -> rollback & monitoring; Mariana (Serving Eng) -> patch; QE -> test coverage; ETA for patch: 2026-03-18
resolution: Rollback applied 2026-03-10 and temporary dedup window increased. Post-rollback monitoring shows p99 for affected routes returned to baseline within 3 hours. Patch in review: github.com/redwood/inference-runtime/pull/2798 addresses key normalization and dedup behavior.
follow_up_actions: 1) Run 72-hour monitoring window and validate no recurrence (owner: Derek)
2) Deploy normalization patch behind feature flag to staging for load test (owner: Mariana)
3) Coordinate with LexaHealth CS to review incident, provide timeline and compensatory credits if SLA breached (owner: Support Manager)
4) Update runbook describing kernel-selector rollout checklist to include cache compatibility validation (owner: EngOps)
5) Schedule postmortem within 7 days and link to incident page
